source_notes: Loughborough University's Biomedical Engineering BEng (Hons) programme page (course overview, real entry requirements and the real year-by-year compulsory/optional module titles) was read live at lboro.ac.uk on 2026-09-27. Loughborough's own internal module-by-module syllabus content (detailed learning outcomes, week-by-week content, reading lists) sits behind its module catalogue/student portal and was not accessible; everywhere this course itemises a topic under a real Loughborough module title (e.g. Anatomy and Physiology, Biomaterials 1, Healthcare Engineering), the content taught is the standard, well-established topic breakdown for that biomedical-engineering subject area found in any BEng-level biomedical/bioengineering textbook or module descriptor (e.g. Enderle & Bronzino 'Introduction to Biomedical Engineering'; Ratner et al. 'Biomaterials Science'; Nordin & Frankel 'Basic Biomechanics of the Musculoskeletal System'; Webster 'Medical Instrumentation') -- this is core biomedical-engineering knowledge, not institution-specific content -- cross-checked against the QAA Subject Benchmark Statement for Engineering (5th edition, March 2023, which sets generic threshold learning outcomes across science/mathematics/engineering principles, engineering analysis, design/creativity/innovation, professional practice and values, and teamwork/communication, and does not itemise biomedical engineering as a named sub-discipline, leaving specialist content to individual institutions). Every numerical worked example and mark-scheme value was computed with Python when the course was built; short-answer test items are original, in the style of a UK engineering degree's structured written papers, marked M/A/B as in this library's other STEM courses, never real Loughborough assessment questions (which were not accessible).
